newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel sentiment weakens with crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel sentiment weakens with crude.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel oil prices were little changed on Wednesday, but traders said weaker crude markets were giving rise to weaker sentiment and demand was thin.
North Sea low sulphur product valued steady around $112 a tonne but buyers and sellers remained at stand-off. Russian E4 cargoes were also pegged steady around $102.50.

In the Mediterranean straight-run markets were stable with players awaiting news of long-term Tunisian tender for mid-April and spot Tunisian and Egyptian tenders, for late month loading, due to be awarded on Wednesday.
Traders said there was good availability of Russian high sulphur straight-run cargoes from the Black Sea.
Two M100 cargoes were seen on offer at around $4 over cif one percent sulphur quotes.
Traders said buying interest for most grades was relaxed.
